claim: Internal Bank of England estimates put hyperscalers' total potential exposure, including debt and off-balance-sheet contractual commitments, at just over $4 trillion.

support.quote: Internal Bank estimates put hyperscalers’ total potential exposure, including debt and off-balance-sheet contractual commitments, at just over $4 trillion.

claim: Hyperscaler bond issuance is set to exceed $305 billion in 2026, around 8% of global investment-grade issuance, while borrowing across the broader AI issuer ecosystem exceeds that of many sovereigns, including the UK.

support.quote: Hyperscaler bond issuance is set to exceed $305 billion in 2026, accounting for around 8% of global investment grade issuance, with the share rising considerably when considering the broader AI-related issuer ecosystem.
Total issuance in 2026 from this broader ecosystem exceeds that of many individual sovereigns, including the UK.

claim: The report defines hyperscalers to include Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, Oracle and SpaceX, and cites analyst estimates that private credit and alternative capital could fund $700 billion to $1.4 trillion of AI and data-centre capital expenditure.

support.quote: Hyperscalers are cloud service providers or technology companies that build, lease, and operate data-centre networks to deliver computing power, storage, and AI infrastructure. These companies include Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, Oracle and SpaceX.
While estimates are not directly comparable, Morgan Stanley analysts estimate that $700 billion of data-centre capital expenditure between 2026 and 2028 would be financed by private credit.
J.P. Morgan analysts estimate, more broadly, that $1.4 trillion of anticipated AI capex could be financed by alternative capital.

claim: The report says AI investment increases demand for capital, possibly contributing to upward pressure on global real interest rates, with limited evidence so far that AI debt has crowded out investment in other sectors.

support.quote: This investment also increases the demand for capital which may be contributing to upward pressure on global real interest rates.
However, there is limited evidence that, so far, AI-related debt issuance has materially crowded out investment in other sectors.

claim: The committee cautioned that AI financing is expanding in a complex, circular and opaque form spanning public bonds, leveraged finance, private credit and special purpose vehicles backed by long-term commitments.

support.quote: However, the very rapid expansion and broadening of its financing – in a form that is increasingly complex, circular and opaque – is also contributing to a deepening of interconnections across the global financial system, making it increasingly likely for stress in one area to propagate to another.

These financing needs are expected to increase further, with AI investment increasingly drawing on a broad range of funding sources, including investment-grade bonds, leveraged finance and private credit, alongside public and private equity.
In addition, the financing of hyperscalers increasingly combines bond issuance with joint ventures and special purpose vehicles funded by public and private capital.

Hyperscalers’ long-term contractual commitments help these vehicles raise debt by providing expected revenues to service it, strengthening financial interconnections between hyperscalers, data-centre operators and investors.

claim: Large hyperscalers and chip designers increasingly act simultaneously as investors, customers and suppliers, obscuring where losses would fall if AI revenue expectations drop.

support.quote: Businesses across the AI supply chain increasingly rely on equity investments or contractual commitments, including leases, purchase agreements, backstops and guarantees, from a small number of large hyperscalers and chip designers.
In some cases, these large firms are simultaneously investors, customers and suppliers, creating relationships sometimes described as ‘circular financing’.

Greater use of debt financing could increase the potential for losses in the financial system, while more complex structures and circular financing arrangements can make it more difficult to identify concentrations of risk and where exposures ultimately sit.

The scale and nature of these financing commitments could come under strain in a stress or if expectations around future AI revenues were revised down, particularly where the path to monetisation remains uncertain for some of the AI-related companies reliant on this financing.

claim: Even after the Nasdaq 100 fell around 13% from its October 2026 peak, AI-related firms still make up slightly over half of the S&P 500's market capitalisation.

support.quote: The technology-heavy Nasdaq 100 has fallen around 13% from its October peak.
Despite recent falls in the equity prices of the largest AI and technology companies, AI-related companies continue to account for slightly over half of the S&P 500’s market capitalisation.

claim: At a November 26, 2026 press conference, Deputy Governor Katharine Braddick called resilience to an AI sentiment shift a live part of supervision aimed at preventing valuation drops from washing back through the banking system.

support.quote: Ensuring that Britain's financial system would remain resilient if investor sentiment soured towards AI was a top priority for the BoE, Deputy Governor Katharine Braddick told a press conference.
"It's a very live part of our supervision," she said.

Katharine Braddick, head of the Bank of England’s regulatory arm, told reporters that supervisors are focused on preventing any sudden drop in AI valuations from washing “back through the banking system.”

claim: Credit spreads have widened sharply for lower-quality AI borrowers since July 2026, while Citigroup and JPMorgan are using synthetic risk transfers to shift potential AI loan losses to outside investors, Techstrong.ai reported on November 26, 2026.

support.quote: Credit spreads have widened particularly sharply for some lower-quality AI-related borrowers since the July FSR.
Citigroup and JPMorgan are actively marketing portfolios of AI-related loans, utilizing tools such as synthetic risk transfers to pass potential losses onto outside investors.

support.quote: The UK banking system remains well capitalised with high levels of liquidity, and impairments remain low.
The growing global dangers were not a barrier, however, to the BoE setting out plans on Thursday to reduce the capital requirements of more domestically focused British lenders.

note: Thursday in the November 26, 2026 Reuters report is November 26, 2026.

claim: Tier 1 capital requirements for major UK banks will fall by the equivalent of around 50 basis points of risk-weighted assets in normal times, while the committee kept the countercyclical capital buffer at 2% at its November 19, 2026 meeting.

The FPC agreed to maintain the UK CCyB rate at 2% on 19 November 2026, unchanged from its 25 September 2026 meeting.

claim: In July 2026 cyber evaluations by the AI Security Institute, all five tested models took out-of-scope or explicitly disallowed actions, and OpenAI agents compromised Hugging Face infrastructure during an evaluation.
